every prompt opens 'Gouache painting of <subject>' so the medium sits inside CLIP's ~77-token window; the character's bible signature comes first, then the beat's action, then one style-and-period clause identical in all 138 prompts, opening 'Hand-painted gouache illustration' with visible brushwork and matte paper grain (bicharak r4 fix for the oil-realist drift)

light is fixed positively in the shared clause: 'lit only by oil lamps, candles, moon and sun'; light sources named in beats are period objects (glass-chimney kerosene lamp, clay oil lamp, oil lanterns, oil signal lamp, candle-cup chandelier, oil headlamp of a steam locomotive)

clean-shaven anchors in the bicharak r7 judge style: the narrator 'clean-shaven with a smooth bare chin and smooth bare upper lip'; the storyteller and all three collector looks 'smooth shaven chin and cheeks' after the bible's moustache signature; the relative 'a thin moustache over a smooth shaven chin'. lettering-prone nouns are kept only where the beat needs them and are made blank or turned away: letter of appointment -> folded paper with a red wax seal; Persian book of verse -> recited from memory, small closed leather-bound book; notebook pages tilted away; half-written report -> sheets lying face down; newspaper held with its plain grey back to the viewer; letters -> sealed envelopes; ledgers closed and cloth-bound; flying pages blank ivory parchment; railway platform walls plain whitewashed

period anchors where beats could drift: 'wooden-bodied 1890s Indian railway compartment with slatted teak benches and a ceiling oil lamp', 1890s steam locomotive, 'Deccan-sultanate white marble palace' with pointed carved arches and jali screens, Deccan court, Nizam's government in Hyderabad, and the shared 'Nizam-era Hyderabad state, Deccan India, 1890s'
